csharp.message: visual scripts are not compiled by the C# engine yet: they will compile to C# with the script host (docs/csharp-redesign.md, stage 4); until then the Rust engine (rust/) compiles them and finds their problems

why: The Rust engine compiles a visual script to WebAssembly to find its problems; the C# engine's scripts are C#, and visual scripts compile to C# with the script host (stage 4). Until then a visual script's problems say it is not compiled rather than that nothing is wrong (AGENTS.md rule 15).

script-every-field.bscript is not a valid script: bayleaf_describe: inspector: "speed": choices are for a whole number (by place) or a text, not a Number
why: As for step 2; the script host's refusal of its Inspector options is the same in both engines.

play.start says how the scripts run. The Rust engine interprets them by default (wasmi) and compiles them with wasmtime when asked; the C# engine's scripts are C#, always compiled (Roslyn, then .NET's JIT), so it says compiled whichever is asked. The rest of play.start's result is the same.
